slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's AI-assisted country review says its searches of State Department, UNODC, World Bank and government sources found no evidence of a digital case management, incident reporting or records system for the police or the gendarmerie, and no pilot or donor project for police digitalisation; it gives no date, so the publication date is used.

The essay's AI-assisted country review says complaints are filed in person and rural stations 'likely' use handwritten procès-verbaux, an inference from finding no contrary evidence rather than a sourced statement; it gives no date, so the publication date is used.

note: The document's own header marks its country figures as an AI-aided compilation, not sourced fact, and study.json lists it under exclude_sources. It names no police information system; it says criminal record certificates are issued manually by the Ministry of Justice.

A Gabonese Council of Ministers communiqué; the term hit is the 'Haut-Commissariat' for the Belinga project. It mentions Equatorial Guinea only for three telecoms accords with Gabon (roaming, border interference, fibre interconnection) and states nothing about police or gendarmerie records.

systems.country_label: Proyecto de Implementación de un Sistema de Interconexión de las Comisarías de Policías
systems.tiers: police stations (comisarías); no number or location stated
projects to interconnect its databases with the embassies, to migrate them, and to extend CNEDOGE to the provincial capitals

note: No fact: the 2026 budget law lists, under the Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional's Programa de Reforzamiento (16A), project 006 to implement a system interconnecting the police stations, with no statement that stations record reports or cases in it. The passage's amount column is misaligned in the extract (005 and 006 sit beside figures of 25, unit not shown), so no amount is given. Also listed: a ministry web page (003), complaint boxes in stations (010), and Policía Nacional staffing lines.

systems.country_label: digitalización integral del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional
systems.tiers: the ministry; said to cover police processes, human resources management, administration and archive; no station or tier stated

systems.country_label: Centro Nacional de Emisión de Documentos de Guinea Ecuatorial (CNEDOGE)

note: No fact: on 2025-05-09 the Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional put to the Finance Ministry's budget conference, as proposals for 2026 still to be prioritised, a whole-ministry digitalisation 'including police processes', HR, administration and archive, and the reactivation of the criminal database (AFIS). It does not say that stations record reports or cases digitally, so the digitalisation is unclassified; AFIS needing reactivation is an identification-class statement. Comisarías are named only for revenue measures (a set amount per station, Treasury collection points in each).

No fact: the statement says no government agency is responsible for maintaining criminal records and that the Ministry of Justice issues a favourable certificate to anyone paying the fee (2025). That is an absence in the identification class, not a statement about station records, and it names no police information system.

No fact: the passages of Law 7/2024 name the Policía Nacional only as an authority that preserves data in an information system under investigation (art. 57) and applies for judicial authorisation to obtain it (art. 59). The law states nothing about the police's own records or systems.
No fact: the passages name Equatorial Guinea only as FOCAC co-chair for 2027 to 2030 (para 11.4). Nothing on police or gendarmerie records in the country.

systems.country_label: database of information on persons who have been prosecuted and convicted by the criminal courts

systems.tiers: an aim of the directorate's action plan for fiscal year 2022; the report does not say it was built

note: No fact: the state's UPR report names the National Police and gendarmerie only for human rights training (200 officers in 2021), inspections of 10 police holding facilities and gendarmerie stations in 2019-2021, and four trafficking cases referred by the criminal investigation brigade. The one system near the field is the prisons directorate's planned 2022 database of convicted persons; a planned referral and case management system for gender-based violence (2024 workshop, Ministry of Social Affairs) is outside the police.

consulted to check that a passport applicant never held an identity document (DIP); the order does not say whether it is paper or digital

note: No fact: the order of 2022-06-22 sets the procedure for biometric passports applied for abroad. The Policía Nacional appears as reviewer of uploaded applications and keeper of an archive of identity documents; nothing is said of stations recording reports or cases. Art. 15 requires a lost or stolen passport to be reported to the authorities of the jurisdiction, with no means stated; art. 16 has CNEDOGE notify annulments to migration authorities and INTERPOL.

No fact: a news report of 2026-08-22 on a Gendarmería Nacional investigation into a contract of more than 425 million CFA francs to equip the UNGE computer room in Bata. The gendarmerie is the investigator; the computers are the university's. Nothing on police or gendarmerie records or systems.

State press office, 10 November 2023: launch of CNIAPGE's Plataforma de Digitalización de Expedientes, an administrative case-file platform started in the Presidencia del Gobierno and the Ministerio de Justicia y Asuntos Sociales. General public administration; no police, gendarmerie or station is mentioned, so no system in the study's field.
